title: Transient Limiter Outage Recovery Agent - SLO-preserving soft-admission and cross-region reconciliation
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Background: Recent incidents show that transient outages of the global limiter control plane can cause either hard denials (customers blocked) or uncontrolled open-admit behavior during failover windows, both of which cause SLO violations. Problem statement: we need a mechanism to bridge short-lived limiter outages without violating latency and error SLOs and while preserving per-tenant fairness and billing correctness. Goal: design and implement a locally-run Recovery Agent that proxies admission decisions when the primary quota store is unavailable. The Agent must be SLO-aware (maintain p50/p95/p99 latency budgets), tenant-aware (avoid starvation), and reconciliatory (merge local state back to global quota store after recovery). Core idea: a soft-admission proxy with three coupled capabilities: 1) Latency-aware admission: per-tenant residual latency budget tokens determine how aggressively we admit requests; Agent tracks observed latencies and reduces admission probability for tenants nearing their latency budgets. 2) Probabilistic credit aging: instead of fixed bursts, local credits age with a decay curve and admission is sampled probabilistically to avoid synchronized spikes. 3) Cross-region reconciliation: after limiter recovery, local ledgers exchange digestable deltas and reconcile via idempotent operations and tombstone markers to avoid double-counting. Important safety features: circuit breaker thresholds, global kill-switch (operator-controlled), and conservative default admission that favors preserving latency over raw throughput. This ticket scopes the design, prototype, and initial canary on one region, with telemetry and failback automation.
acceptance_criteria: Agent runs in degraded mode and admits traffic with probabilistic sampling when global limiter is unreachable
During a simulated limiter outage (30s to 5m), platform p95 token generation latency increases by no more than 2x compared to healthy baseline
Error rate for admitted requests in degraded mode does not exceed 1.5x baseline and overall customer-facing SLO violations remain within incident severity targets
Per-tenant fairness test: no tenant receives >3x of their baseline proportion of admitted requests during a 5 minute degraded window (validated via synthetic workload)
Reconciliation is idempotent: applying local deltas to the global quota store after recovery results in consistent final quotas with no over-crediting (end-to-end integration test)
Observability: Grafana dashboard surfaces degraded-mode flag, admission-rate by tenant, latency-budget headroom, and reconciliation status
Runbook entry and operator kill-switch are documented and validated in chaos tests

comments: 2026-02-10 Priya Natarajan: Initial triage after 2026-02-08 limiter outage. Root cause: regional lease expiry + slow quorum re-establishment. Proposal: local soft-admit agent to reduce hard-denies and uncontrolled open-admit windows.

2026-02-14 Design review: PM (Jasmine Cole) requests strict customer-impact thresholds and explicit billing semantics during degraded mode; added acceptance criteria for fairness and billing idempotency.

2026-02-18 Engineering sync: decided to use probabilistic admission with token aging rather than deterministic rationing to avoid large synchronized spikes noted in prior incidents (ENG-27183 referenced).

2026-02-22 Perf bench (local): prototype Agent admitted 30k rps of mixed tenants with p95 latency increase ~1.8x under synthetic load; observed skew for high-weight tenants, added corrective weight-normalization step.

2026-02-25 Security/Compliance note: security reviewed admission pathway; no direct data exfiltration risk identified. Finance asked for clear billing reconciliation to avoid double-billing; added idempotent reconciliation requirement.
2026-02-27 PM feedback: add 'grace window' configuration per product tier so premium customers can be prioritized in congested degraded windows; updated tasks.
2026-02-28 PR created: github.com/redwood/recovery-agent/pull/12 - initial policy implementation and sampler. Link: https://github.com/redwood/recovery-agent/pull/12
